# UPS is hiring 100,000 seasonal workers for the holidays, down for the second year in a row

The company hired 110,000 seasonal workers in 2025 and 125,000 in 2024, as it continues to shrink its workforce and close facilities

By Cris Tolomia· 2 min read· Updated October 7, 2026

John Keeble/Getty Images

UPS announced plans to hire 100,000 seasonal workers ahead of the 2026 holiday shipping season, continuing a two-year decline in temporary staffing as the company restructures its operations.

The seasonal workforce will sort, transport, and deliver packages during the holiday rush, UPS said. The company said applicants can receive a job offer in less than seven minutes, and that seasonal roles come with competitive pay, flexible schedules, and the possibility of a permanent position.

The 100,000 target marks a reduction from each of the previous two years. UPS hired 110,000 seasonal workers in 2025 — itself a drop of 15,000 from the 125,000 it brought on in 2024, according to Reuters.
